newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices move higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices move higher.

text.p: Millfeed prices were higher Monday at several locations and dealers reported strong demand for prompt-shipped material.

Millfeed production was expected to slip this week and next because many flour mills will be shut down during the three-day U.S. Labor Day holiday weekend. In addition, flour mills have sold much of their upcoming production and commanded higher prices for any new sales.
Higher CBOT corn futures buoyed millfeed values in a few areas, but several sources said millfeed prices appear to be rising independently of corn.

In the southeast U.S., dealers said feed mixers continued to buy millfeeds to mix with corn for hog and poultry rations. Corn harvest was under way in the Southeast and good yields were reported, however grain moisture levels remain high.
The closely-watched Kansas City rail market was higher, with bids and offers up $2.00 at $116 and $118 per ton, respectively.
